module Statemachine
  ARROW = '=>>'
  ON = 'upon'
  STATE = 'mode'
  ACT = 'run'
  HAS_GUARDS = true
  HAS_HIER = false
  LET = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_'
  DIG = '0123456789'
  OPS = %w[< <= > >= == !=]

  def self.ident?(s)
    !s.empty? && LET.include?(s[0]) && s.each_char.all? { |c| LET.include?(c) || DIG.include?(c) }
  end

  def self.integer?(s)
    body = s[0] == '-' ? s[1..] : s
    !body.empty? && body.length <= 6 && body.each_char.all? { |c| DIG.include?(c) }
  end

  def self.parse_actions(text)
    return nil if text.strip.empty?
    acts = []
    text.split(',', -1).each do |piece|
      w = piece.split
      return nil if w.empty?
      v = w[0]
      if v == 'emit' && w.length == 2 && ident?(w[1])
        acts << ['emit', w[1], 0]
      elsif v == 'set' && w.length == 3 && ident?(w[1]) && integer?(w[2])
        acts << ['set', w[1], w[2].to_i]
      elsif (v == 'inc' || v == 'dec') && [2, 3].include?(w.length) && ident?(w[1]) && (w.length == 2 || integer?(w[2]))
        amt = w.length == 3 ? w[2].to_i : 1
        acts << ['add', w[1], v == 'inc' ? amt : -amt]
      else
        return nil
      end
    end
    acts
  end

  def self.parse(defn)
    states = {}
    errs = []
    refs = []
    initial = nil
    cur = nil
    defn.split("\n", -1).each_with_index do |raw, idx|
      no = idx + 1
      w = raw.split('#', 2)[0].to_s.split
      next if w.empty?
      k = w[0]
      if k == STATE
        ok = w.length == 2 || (HAS_HIER && w.length == 4 && w[2] == '<')
        if !ok || !ident?(w[1]) || (w.length == 4 && !ident?(w[3]))
          errs << [no, 'bad state']
        elsif states.key?(w[1])
          errs << [no, 'duplicate state']
        else
          parent = w.length == 4 ? w[3] : nil
          states[w[1]] = { line: no, parent: parent, trans: [], enter: [], exit: [] }
          refs << [no, parent] if parent
          cur = w[1]
        end
      elsif k == 'initial'
        if w.length != 2 || !ident?(w[1])
          errs << [no, 'bad initial']
        elsif !initial.nil?
          errs << [no, 'duplicate initial']
        else
          initial = w[1]
          refs << [no, w[1]]
        end
      elsif k == ON || (HAS_GUARDS && (k == 'enter' || k == 'exit'))
        if cur.nil?
          errs << [no, 'outside state']
          next
        end
        if k == 'enter' || k == 'exit'
          acts = parse_actions(w[1..].join(' '))
          if acts.nil?
            errs << [no, 'bad action']
          else
            states[cur][k.to_sym].concat(acts)
          end
          next
        end
        v = w[1..]
        guard = nil
        i = 1
        if v.length < 3 || !ident?(v[0])
          errs << [no, 'bad transition']
          next
        end
        if v[1] == 'if'
          if !HAS_GUARDS || v.length < 5 || !ident?(v[2]) || !OPS.include?(v[3]) || !integer?(v[4])
            errs << [no, 'bad transition']
            next
          end
          guard = [v[2], v[3], v[4].to_i]
          i = 5
        end
        if i >= v.length || v[i] != ARROW || i + 1 >= v.length || !ident?(v[i + 1])
          errs << [no, 'bad transition']
          next
        end
        target = v[i + 1]
        rest = v[(i + 2)..]
        acts = []
        unless rest.empty?
          if rest[0] != ACT
            errs << [no, 'bad transition']
            next
          end
          acts = parse_actions(rest[1..].join(' '))
          if acts.nil?
            errs << [no, 'bad action']
            next
          end
        end
        states[cur][:trans] << [v[0], guard, target, acts]
        refs << [no, target]
      else
        errs << [no, 'unknown directive']
      end
    end
    refs.each { |no, name| errs << [no, 'unknown state'] unless states.key?(name) }
    states.each do |name, s|
      seen = {}
      x = name
      while !x.nil? && states.key?(x) && !seen[x]
        seen[x] = true
        x = states[x][:parent]
      end
      errs << [s[:line], 'parent cycle'] if !x.nil? && seen[x]
    end
    unless errs.empty?
      e = errs.min
      return [nil, "error: line #{e[0]}: #{e[1]}"]
    end
    return [nil, 'error: no initial state'] if initial.nil?
    [[states, initial], nil]
  end

  def self.ancestors(states, name)
    out = []
    p = states[name][:parent]
    until p.nil?
      out << p
      p = states[p][:parent]
    end
    out
  end

  def self.machine(defn, events)
    parsed, err = parse(defn)
    return err if err
    states, initial = parsed
    counters = {}
    touched = {}
    emitted = []
    run = lambda do |acts|
      acts.each do |kind, name, val|
        if kind == 'emit'
          emitted << name
        elsif kind == 'set'
          counters[name] = val
          touched[name] = true
        else
          counters[name] = (counters[name] || 0) + val
          touched[name] = true
        end
      end
    end
    fmt = ->(text) { emitted.empty? ? text : "#{text} | #{emitted.join(' ')}" }
    out = []
    (ancestors(states, initial).reverse + [initial]).each { |s| run.call(states[s][:enter]) }
    out << fmt.call("start: -> #{initial}")
    state = initial
    events.split.each do |e|
      emitted = []
      fired = nil
      a = state
      while !a.nil? && fired.nil?
        states[a][:trans].each do |t|
          next if t[0] != e
          ok = true
          if t[1]
            v = counters[t[1][0]] || 0
            n = t[1][2]
            ok = case t[1][1]
                 when '<' then v < n
                 when '<=' then v <= n
                 when '>' then v > n
                 when '>=' then v >= n
                 when '==' then v == n
                 else v != n
                 end
          end
          if ok
            fired = t
            break
          end
        end
        a = states[a][:parent]
      end
      if fired.nil?
        out << "#{e}: ignored"
        next
      end
      target = fired[2]
      anc_t = ancestors(states, target)
      lca = ancestors(states, state).find { |x| anc_t.include?(x) }
      exits = []
      x = state
      while x != lca
        exits << x
        x = states[x][:parent]
      end
      enters = []
      x = target
      while x != lca
        enters << x
        x = states[x][:parent]
      end
      enters.reverse!
      exits.each { |s| run.call(states[s][:exit]) }
      run.call(fired[3])
      enters.each { |s| run.call(states[s][:enter]) }
      out << fmt.call("#{e}: #{state} -> #{target}")
      state = target
    end
    out << ('final ' + state + touched.keys.sort.map { |n| " #{n}=#{counters[n]}" }.join)
    out.join("\n")
  end
end

start.README.md:
# Machine runner for a library lending desk

The firmware team describes a library lending desk in a small text language and wants to *replay* event logs against it. `machine(definition, events)` parses the definition, starts the machine, feeds it the events and returns a trace. This document is the whole language.

## Definition language

The definition is text with one directive per line (lines are separated by `\n`; line numbers count from 1). On every line everything from a `#` on is a comment. The rest is split into *words* at blanks (spaces and tabs); a line without words is ignored. The first word chooses the directive. A **name** (state, event or counter) is an *identifier*: a letter or `_`, followed by letters, digits or `_` (ASCII only, case-sensitive).

* `mode NAME`: declares a state and makes it the *current declaration*; the directives below belong to it until the next `mode` line. States may be declared in any order.
* `initial NAME`: the state the machine starts in (exactly one such line).
* `upon EVENT [if VAR OP NUMBER] =>> TARGET [run ACTIONS]`: a transition of the current declaration: when `EVENT` arrives and the guard holds, the machine moves to `TARGET`, running the actions.
* `enter ACTIONS` and `exit ACTIONS`: actions run when the machine enters or leaves the current declaration (several lines of the same kind accumulate, in order).

**Actions** are separated by commas (a comma never occurs inside an action); each one is, with `VAR` a name and `N` an integer written as optional `-` and one to six ASCII digits:

* `emit NAME`: add `NAME` to the output of the current step;
* `set VAR N`: set the counter `VAR` to `N`;
* `inc VAR [N]` / `dec VAR [N]`: add or subtract `N` (default 1) to the counter. Counters that were never set are 0.

A **guard** compares a counter with a constant: `OP` is one of `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `==`, `!=`, and `NUMBER` an integer as above. A guard is true when the counter's current value satisfies the comparison.

`=>>`, `run`, `if` and the comparison operators are words of their own: they must be separated from their neighbours by blanks.

## Errors in the definition

Every line is checked on its own; if any line has a problem the result of `machine` is just `error: line N: REASON` for the problem on the **lowest line number** (nothing runs). A line has at most one problem. The reasons:

| reason | when |
|---|---|
| `unknown directive` | the first word is not a directive of this language |
| `bad state` | a `mode` line with the wrong shape or an invalid name |
| `duplicate state` | a second declaration of an already declared state |
| `bad initial` | an `initial` line with the wrong shape or an invalid name |
| `duplicate initial` | a second valid `initial` line |
| `outside state` | a `upon`, `enter` or `exit` line before the first valid `mode` line |
| `bad transition` | a transition line that does not have the shape above (missing words, invalid names, wrong arrow or action separator word, bad guard) |
| `bad action` | an action list that is empty (also `run` followed by nothing) or has an empty or malformed action, in a transition or in an `enter`/`exit` line |
| `unknown state` | a reference (`initial`, a transition target) to a state that is declared nowhere in the definition; reported on the line of the reference |

For a transition line, shape problems (`bad transition`) are judged first and the action list (`bad action`) afterwards. A line that causes `bad state`, `duplicate state`, `bad transition` or `bad action` is ignored otherwise (it declares nothing). If there are no line problems but no `initial` line at all, the result is `error: no initial state`.

## Running

`events` is text split into events at blanks (spaces, tabs, newlines); any word is an event name (no validation). The machine starts by *entering* the initial state (its `enter` actions), then handles each event in turn:

1. The transitions of the current state are examined in declaration order; the **first** one with the right event whose guard (if any) is true fires. If no transition fires at all, the event is *ignored* (nothing changes).
2. A transition that fires moves the machine from the current state `S` to `TARGET`. Guards use the counter values from *before* the step.
3. Running order: the `exit` actions of `S`, then the actions of the transition, then the `enter` actions of `TARGET`. A transition to the current state leaves and re-enters it.

## Trace

The result is lines joined by `\n` (no trailing newline):

* first `start: -> INITIAL`;
* then one line per event, `EVENT: S -> TARGET` when a transition fired and `EVENT: ignored` otherwise;
* a line that ran any `emit` actions (during entering at the start, or during the step) ends with ` | ` and the emitted names separated by single spaces, in the order they were emitted;
* last `final STATE` followed, for every counter that was ever the subject of `set`, `inc` or `dec` (even if its value is 0 again), by ` NAME=VALUE`, sorted by name in ascending byte order.

## Interface

Implement this function in `lib/statemachine.rb` (module `Statemachine`):

```
Statemachine.machine(definition, events)
```

* `definition`: the machine definition text
* `events`: the events, separated by blanks
* returns the trace text, or an `error: ...` line.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

Definition:

```
initial free
mode free
  upon borrow =>> reserved run emit beep
mode reserved
  upon return =>> free
```

Events: `borrow reserve return`

Result:

```
start: -> free
borrow: free -> reserved | beep
reserve: ignored
return: reserved -> free
final free
```

Definition:

```
initial reserved
mode reserved
  enter set n 0
  upon fine if tries > 2 =>> lent run set tries 2
mode overdue
  upon borrow =>> overdue run emit lock, emit flash
  upon borrow =>> overdue
mode lent
  upon reserve if tries >= 3 =>> reserved run dec count
```

Events: `fine reserve audit remind return fine`

Result:

```
start: -> reserved
fine: ignored
reserve: ignored
audit: ignored
remind: ignored
return: ignored
fine: ignored
final reserved n=0
```

Definition:

```
initial reserved
mode reserved
  enter set n -2
  upon return if tries > -1 =>> free run emit close, emit hum
mode free
  upon remind =>> reserved
  upon return =>> lent run dec hits, emit alert
mode lost
  upon return =>> lent run emit report
  upon fine =>> free
mode lent
  enter emit hum, emit beep
  upon remind =>> lost
```

Events: `audit borrow fine audit remind remind audit`

Result:

```
start: -> reserved
audit: ignored
borrow: ignored
fine: ignored
audit: ignored
remind: ignored
remind: ignored
audit: ignored
final reserved n=-2
```

# Machine runner for a library lending desk

The firmware team describes a library lending desk in a small text language and wants to *replay* event logs against it. `machine(definition, events)` parses the definition, starts the machine, feeds it the events and returns a trace. This document is the whole language.

## Definition language

The definition is text with one directive per line (lines are separated by `\n`; line numbers count from 1). On every line everything from a `#` on is a comment. The rest is split into *words* at blanks (spaces and tabs); a line without words is ignored. The first word chooses the directive. A **name** (state, event or counter) is an *identifier*: a letter or `_`, followed by letters, digits or `_` (ASCII only, case-sensitive).

* `state NAME` or `state NAME < PARENT`: declares a state and makes it the *current declaration*; the directives below belong to it until the next `state` line. States may be declared in any order. `< PARENT` makes `PARENT` its parent state (see Hierarchy).
* `initial NAME`: the state the machine starts in (exactly one such line).
* `on EVENT [if VAR OP NUMBER] >> TARGET [do ACTIONS]`: a transition of the current declaration: when `EVENT` arrives and the guard holds, the machine moves to `TARGET`, running the actions.
* `enter ACTIONS` and `exit ACTIONS`: actions run when the machine enters or leaves the current declaration (several lines of the same kind accumulate, in order).

**Actions** are separated by commas (a comma never occurs inside an action); each one is, with `VAR` a name and `N` an integer written as optional `-` and one to six ASCII digits:

* `emit NAME`: add `NAME` to the output of the current step;
* `set VAR N`: set the counter `VAR` to `N`;
* `inc VAR [N]` / `dec VAR [N]`: add or subtract `N` (default 1) to the counter. Counters that were never set are 0.

A **guard** compares a counter with a constant: `OP` is one of `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `==`, `!=`, and `NUMBER` an integer as above. A guard is true when the counter's current value satisfies the comparison.

`>>`, `do`, `if`, `<` and the comparison operators are words of their own: they must be separated from their neighbours by blanks.

## Errors in the definition

Every line is checked on its own; if any line has a problem the result of `machine` is just `error: line N: REASON` for the problem on the **lowest line number** (nothing runs). A line has at most one problem. The reasons:

| reason | when |
|---|---|
| `unknown directive` | the first word is not a directive of this language |
| `bad state` | a `state` line with the wrong shape or an invalid name |
| `duplicate state` | a second declaration of an already declared state |
| `bad initial` | an `initial` line with the wrong shape or an invalid name |
| `duplicate initial` | a second valid `initial` line |
| `outside state` | a `on`, `enter` or `exit` line before the first valid `state` line |
| `bad transition` | a transition line that does not have the shape above (missing words, invalid names, wrong arrow or action separator word, bad guard) |
| `bad action` | an action list that is empty (also `do` followed by nothing) or has an empty or malformed action, in a transition or in an `enter`/`exit` line |
| `unknown state` | a reference (`initial`, a transition target or a parent) to a state that is declared nowhere in the definition; reported on the line of the reference |
| `parent cycle` | the state's chain of parents comes back to a state already visited (a state that is its own parent, or two states that are each other's ancestors); reported on the declaration line of each state of the cycle |

For a transition line, shape problems (`bad transition`) are judged first and the action list (`bad action`) afterwards. A line that causes `bad state`, `duplicate state`, `bad transition` or `bad action` is ignored otherwise (it declares nothing). If there are no line problems but no `initial` line at all, the result is `error: no initial state`.

## Running

`events` is text split into events at blanks (spaces, tabs, newlines); any word is an event name (no validation). The machine starts by *entering* the initial state (the `enter` actions of its ancestors, outermost first, then its own), then handles each event in turn:

1. The transitions of the current state are examined in declaration order; the **first** one with the right event whose guard (if any) is true fires. If none of them fires, the transitions of its parent are examined the same way, then those of its grandparent, and so on. If no transition fires at all, the event is *ignored* (nothing changes).
2. A transition that fires moves the machine from the current state `S` to `TARGET` (the transition may be declared in an ancestor of `S`, but the machine always leaves from `S`). Guards use the counter values from *before* the step.
3. **Exits and enters.** Let `L` be the lowest state that is a *proper* ancestor of both `S` and `TARGET` (there may be none). The machine leaves `S`, then its parent, and so on **up to but not including** `L`, running each state's `exit` actions in that order (innermost first). Then the transition's own actions run. Then it enters the states on the path from just below `L` down to `TARGET` (outermost first), running their `enter` actions. So a transition to the current state leaves and re-enters it, and a transition to an ancestor leaves the state and re-enters the ancestor.

## Trace

The result is lines joined by `\n` (no trailing newline):

* first `start: -> INITIAL`;
* then one line per event, `EVENT: S -> TARGET` when a transition fired and `EVENT: ignored` otherwise;
* a line that ran any `emit` actions (during entering at the start, or during the step) ends with ` | ` and the emitted names separated by single spaces, in the order they were emitted;
* last `final STATE` followed, for every counter that was ever the subject of `set`, `inc` or `dec` (even if its value is 0 again), by ` NAME=VALUE`, sorted by name in ascending byte order.

## Interface

Implement this function in `src/Statemachine.java` (class `Statemachine`, default package):

```
public static String machine(String definition, String events)
```

* `definition`: the machine definition text
* `events`: the events, separated by blanks
* returns the trace text, or an `error: ...` line.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

Definition:

```
initial free
state free
  on borrow >> reserved do emit beep
state reserved
  on return >> free
```

Events: `borrow reserve return`

Result:

```
start: -> free
borrow: free -> reserved | beep
reserve: ignored
return: reserved -> free
final free
```

Definition:

```
state lost
  on return if count != 2 >> overdue do set count 1, emit alert
state archived < lost
  exit emit report
  on borrow >> overdue
  on reserve >> lost do emit ok, set count 2
state overdue < archived
  on reserve >> lost do emit hum, set hits 1
initial lost
  on borrow >> archived do set hits -3, inc tries
```

Events: `reserve fine fine fine fine borrow`

Result:

```
start: -> lost
reserve: ignored
fine: ignored
fine: ignored
fine: ignored
fine: ignored
borrow: ignored
final lost
```

Definition:

```
initial lent
state lent
  enter emit ring
  exit emit report
  on remind if n < 0 >> lost do inc n 2, emit ok
  on borrow >> lent do emit report, emit unlock
  on reserve if hits != -1 >> lent do emit bad, emit flash
state reserved < lent
  enter emit notify
  on fine >> archived
  on remind if count > -1 >> archived do emit ring
state lost < reserved
  on remind if count > 0 >> archived do inc n
state archived < lent
  on remind if count > 3 >> lost do emit report, emit ring
```

Events: `borrow audit fine borrow remind remind reserve`

Result:

```
start: -> lent | ring
borrow: lent -> lent | report report unlock ring
audit: ignored
fine: ignored
borrow: lent -> lent | report report unlock ring
remind: ignored
remind: ignored
reserve: lent -> lent | report bad flash ring
final lent
```

Run the visible tests with `mkdir -p build && javac -d build $(find . -name '*.java') && java -cp build TestMain`.

start.README.md:
# Machine runner for a ferry-gate controller

The firmware team describes a ferry-gate controller in a small text language and wants to *replay* event logs against it. `machine(definition, events)` parses the definition, starts the machine, feeds it the events and returns a trace. This document is the whole language.

## Definition language

The definition is text with one directive per line (lines are separated by `\n`; line numbers count from 1). On every line everything from a `#` on is a comment. The rest is split into *words* at blanks (spaces and tabs); a line without words is ignored. The first word chooses the directive. A **name** (state, event or counter) is an *identifier*: a letter or `_`, followed by letters, digits or `_` (ASCII only, case-sensitive).

* `state NAME`: declares a state and makes it the *current declaration*; the directives below belong to it until the next `state` line. States may be declared in any order.
* `initial NAME`: the state the machine starts in (exactly one such line).
* `on EVENT => TARGET [/ ACTIONS]`: a transition of the current declaration: when `EVENT` arrives, the machine moves to `TARGET`, running the actions.

**Actions** are separated by commas (a comma never occurs inside an action); each one is, with `VAR` a name and `N` an integer written as optional `-` and one to six ASCII digits:

* `emit NAME`: add `NAME` to the output of the current step;
* `set VAR N`: set the counter `VAR` to `N`;
* `inc VAR [N]` / `dec VAR [N]`: add or subtract `N` (default 1) to the counter. Counters that were never set are 0.

`=>`, `/` are words of their own: they must be separated from their neighbours by blanks.

## Errors in the definition

Every line is checked on its own; if any line has a problem the result of `machine` is just `error: line N: REASON` for the problem on the **lowest line number** (nothing runs). A line has at most one problem. The reasons:

| reason | when |
|---|---|
| `unknown directive` | the first word is not a directive of this language (`enter` and `exit` do not exist here) |
| `bad state` | a `state` line with the wrong shape or an invalid name |
| `duplicate state` | a second declaration of an already declared state |
| `bad initial` | an `initial` line with the wrong shape or an invalid name |
| `duplicate initial` | a second valid `initial` line |
| `outside state` | a `on` line before the first valid `state` line |
| `bad transition` | a transition line that does not have the shape above (missing words, invalid names, wrong arrow or action separator word, bad guard, or a guard where guards do not exist) |
| `bad action` | an action list that is empty (also `/` followed by nothing) or has an empty or malformed action, in a transition |
| `unknown state` | a reference (`initial`, a transition target) to a state that is declared nowhere in the definition; reported on the line of the reference |

For a transition line, shape problems (`bad transition`) are judged first and the action list (`bad action`) afterwards. A line that causes `bad state`, `duplicate state`, `bad transition` or `bad action` is ignored otherwise (it declares nothing). If there are no line problems but no `initial` line at all, the result is `error: no initial state`.

## Running

`events` is text split into events at blanks (spaces, tabs, newlines); any word is an event name (no validation). The machine starts by *entering* the initial state, then handles each event in turn:

1. The transitions of the current state are examined in declaration order; the **first** one with the right event whose guard (if any) is true fires. If no transition fires at all, the event is *ignored* (nothing changes).
2. A transition that fires moves the machine from the current state `S` to `TARGET`. Guards use the counter values from *before* the step.
3. The transition's actions run. A transition to the current state is allowed.

## Trace

The result is lines joined by `\n` (no trailing newline):

* first `start: -> INITIAL`;
* then one line per event, `EVENT: S -> TARGET` when a transition fired and `EVENT: ignored` otherwise;
* a line that ran any `emit` actions (during entering at the start, or during the step) ends with ` | ` and the emitted names separated by single spaces, in the order they were emitted;
* last `final STATE` followed, for every counter that was ever the subject of `set`, `inc` or `dec` (even if its value is 0 again), by ` NAME=VALUE`, sorted by name in ascending byte order.

## Interface

Implement this function in `src/statemachine.js`:

```
function machine(definition, events)  // returns a string; exported with module.exports
```

* `definition`: the machine definition text
* `events`: the events, separated by blanks
* returns the trace text, or an `error: ...` line.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

Definition:

```
initial closed
state closed
  on push => opening / emit beep
state opening
  on timer => closed
```

Events: `push key timer`

Result:

```
start: -> closed
push: closed -> opening | beep
key: ignored
timer: opening -> closed
final closed
```

Definition:

```
initial fault
state fault
  on push => closed / emit ok
state locked
  on reset => fault
  on jam => fault
  on reset => fault
state closed
  on jam => fault
  on reset => closed
```

Events: `timer key wave jam push jam`

Result:

```
start: -> fault
timer: ignored
key: ignored
wave: ignored
jam: ignored
push: fault -> closed | ok
jam: closed -> fault
final fault
```

Definition:

```
state closing
  on jam => closed / emit notify, emit ok
  on jam => closed
state closed
  on jam => opening
state opening
  on key => closed
initial closing
  on jam => opening / emit unlock, emit reset
state open
  on reset => open / emit notify
  on push => opening
```

Events: `timer key reset jam key wave key`

Result:

```
start: -> closing
timer: ignored
key: ignored
reset: ignored
jam: closing -> closed | notify ok
key: ignored
wave: ignored
key: ignored
final closed
```

solution.lib/statemachine.rb:
module Statemachine
  ARROW = '=>'
  ON = 'case'
  STATE = 'state'
  ACT = '!'
  HAS_GUARDS = true
  HAS_HIER = true
  LET = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_'
  DIG = '0123456789'
  OPS = %w[< <= > >= == !=]

  def self.ident?(s)
    !s.empty? && LET.include?(s[0]) && s.each_char.all? { |c| LET.include?(c) || DIG.include?(c) }
  end

  def self.integer?(s)
    body = s[0] == '-' ? s[1..] : s
    !body.empty? && body.length <= 6 && body.each_char.all? { |c| DIG.include?(c) }
  end

  def self.parse_actions(text)
    return nil if text.strip.empty?
    acts = []
    text.split(',', -1).each do |piece|
      w = piece.split
      return nil if w.empty?
      v = w[0]
      if v == 'emit' && w.length == 2 && ident?(w[1])
        acts << ['emit', w[1], 0]
      elsif v == 'set' && w.length == 3 && ident?(w[1]) && integer?(w[2])
        acts << ['set', w[1], w[2].to_i]
      elsif (v == 'inc' || v == 'dec') && [2, 3].include?(w.length) && ident?(w[1]) && (w.length == 2 || integer?(w[2]))
        amt = w.length == 3 ? w[2].to_i : 1
        acts << ['add', w[1], v == 'inc' ? amt : -amt]
      else
        return nil
      end
    end
    acts
  end

  def self.parse(defn)
    states = {}
    errs = []
    refs = []
    initial = nil
    cur = nil
    defn.split("\n", -1).each_with_index do |raw, idx|
      no = idx + 1
      w = raw.split('#', 2)[0].to_s.split
      next if w.empty?
      k = w[0]
      if k == STATE
        ok = w.length == 2 || (HAS_HIER && w.length == 4 && w[2] == '<')
        if !ok || !ident?(w[1]) || (w.length == 4 && !ident?(w[3]))
          errs << [no, 'bad state']
        elsif states.key?(w[1])
          errs << [no, 'duplicate state']
        else
          parent = w.length == 4 ? w[3] : nil
          states[w[1]] = { line: no, parent: parent, trans: [], enter: [], exit: [] }
          refs << [no, parent] if parent
          cur = w[1]
        end
      elsif k == 'initial'
        if w.length != 2 || !ident?(w[1])
          errs << [no, 'bad initial']
        elsif !initial.nil?
          errs << [no, 'duplicate initial']
        else
          initial = w[1]
          refs << [no, w[1]]
        end
      elsif k == ON || (HAS_GUARDS && (k == 'enter' || k == 'exit'))
        if cur.nil?
          errs << [no, 'outside state']
          next
        end
        if k == 'enter' || k == 'exit'
          acts = parse_actions(w[1..].join(' '))
          if acts.nil?
            errs << [no, 'bad action']
          else
            states[cur][k.to_sym].concat(acts)
          end
          next
        end
        v = w[1..]
        guard = nil
        i = 1
        if v.length < 3 || !ident?(v[0])
          errs << [no, 'bad transition']
          next
        end
        if v[1] == 'if'
          if !HAS_GUARDS || v.length < 5 || !ident?(v[2]) || !OPS.include?(v[3]) || !integer?(v[4])
            errs << [no, 'bad transition']
            next
          end
          guard = [v[2], v[3], v[4].to_i]
          i = 5
        end
        if i >= v.length || v[i] != ARROW || i + 1 >= v.length || !ident?(v[i + 1])
          errs << [no, 'bad transition']
          next
        end
        target = v[i + 1]
        rest = v[(i + 2)..]
        acts = []
        unless rest.empty?
          if rest[0] != ACT
            errs << [no, 'bad transition']
            next
          end
          acts = parse_actions(rest[1..].join(' '))
          if acts.nil?
            errs << [no, 'bad action']
            next
          end
        end
        states[cur][:trans] << [v[0], guard, target, acts]
        refs << [no, target]
      else
        errs << [no, 'unknown directive']
      end
    end
    refs.each { |no, name| errs << [no, 'unknown state'] unless states.key?(name) }
    states.each do |name, s|
      seen = {}
      x = name
      while !x.nil? && states.key?(x) && !seen[x]
        seen[x] = true
        x = states[x][:parent]
      end
      errs << [s[:line], 'parent cycle'] if !x.nil? && seen[x]
    end
    unless errs.empty?
      e = errs.min
      return [nil, "error: line #{e[0]}: #{e[1]}"]
    end
    return [nil, 'error: no initial state'] if initial.nil?
    [[states, initial], nil]
  end

  def self.ancestors(states, name)
    out = []
    p = states[name][:parent]
    until p.nil?
      out << p
      p = states[p][:parent]
    end
    out
  end

  def self.machine(defn, events)
    parsed, err = parse(defn)
    return err if err
    states, initial = parsed
    counters = {}
    touched = {}
    emitted = []
    run = lambda do |acts|
      acts.each do |kind, name, val|
        if kind == 'emit'
          emitted << name
        elsif kind == 'set'
          counters[name] = val
          touched[name] = true
        else
          counters[name] = (counters[name] || 0) + val
          touched[name] = true
        end
      end
    end
    fmt = ->(text) { emitted.empty? ? text : "#{text} | #{emitted.join(' ')}" }
    out = []
    (ancestors(states, initial).reverse + [initial]).each { |s| run.call(states[s][:enter]) }
    out << fmt.call("start: -> #{initial}")
    state = initial
    events.split.each do |e|
      emitted = []
      fired = nil
      a = state
      while !a.nil? && fired.nil?
        states[a][:trans].each do |t|
          next if t[0] != e
          ok = true
          if t[1]
            v = counters[t[1][0]] || 0
            n = t[1][2]
            ok = case t[1][1]
                 when '<' then v < n
                 when '<=' then v <= n
                 when '>' then v > n
                 when '>=' then v >= n
                 when '==' then v == n
                 else v != n
                 end
          end
          if ok
            fired = t
            break
          end
        end
        a = states[a][:parent]
      end
      if fired.nil?
        out << "#{e}: ignored"
        next
      end
      target = fired[2]
      anc_t = ancestors(states, target)
      lca = ancestors(states, state).find { |x| anc_t.include?(x) }
      exits = []
      x = state
      while x != lca
        exits << x
        x = states[x][:parent]
      end
      enters = []
      x = target
      while x != lca
        enters << x
        x = states[x][:parent]
      end
      enters.reverse!
      exits.each { |s| run.call(states[s][:exit]) }
      run.call(fired[3])
      enters.each { |s| run.call(states[s][:enter]) }
      out << fmt.call("#{e}: #{state} -> #{target}")
      state = target
    end
    out << ('final ' + state + touched.keys.sort.map { |n| " #{n}=#{counters[n]}" }.join)
    out.join("\n")
  end
end

start.README.md:
# Machine runner for a lighthouse lamp

The firmware team describes a lighthouse lamp in a small text language and wants to *replay* event logs against it. `machine(definition, events)` parses the definition, starts the machine, feeds it the events and returns a trace. This document is the whole language.

## Definition language

The definition is text with one directive per line (lines are separated by `\n`; line numbers count from 1). On every line everything from a `#` on is a comment. The rest is split into *words* at blanks (spaces and tabs); a line without words is ignored. The first word chooses the directive. A **name** (state, event or counter) is an *identifier*: a letter or `_`, followed by letters, digits or `_` (ASCII only, case-sensitive).

* `state NAME` or `state NAME < PARENT`: declares a state and makes it the *current declaration*; the directives below belong to it until the next `state` line. States may be declared in any order. `< PARENT` makes `PARENT` its parent state (see Hierarchy).
* `initial NAME`: the state the machine starts in (exactly one such line).
* `case EVENT [if VAR OP NUMBER] => TARGET [! ACTIONS]`: a transition of the current declaration: when `EVENT` arrives and the guard holds, the machine moves to `TARGET`, running the actions.
* `enter ACTIONS` and `exit ACTIONS`: actions run when the machine enters or leaves the current declaration (several lines of the same kind accumulate, in order).

**Actions** are separated by commas (a comma never occurs inside an action); each one is, with `VAR` a name and `N` an integer written as optional `-` and one to six ASCII digits:

* `emit NAME`: add `NAME` to the output of the current step;
* `set VAR N`: set the counter `VAR` to `N`;
* `inc VAR [N]` / `dec VAR [N]`: add or subtract `N` (default 1) to the counter. Counters that were never set are 0.

A **guard** compares a counter with a constant: `OP` is one of `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `==`, `!=`, and `NUMBER` an integer as above. A guard is true when the counter's current value satisfies the comparison.

`=>`, `!`, `if`, `<` and the comparison operators are words of their own: they must be separated from their neighbours by blanks.

## Errors in the definition

Every line is checked on its own; if any line has a problem the result of `machine` is just `error: line N: REASON` for the problem on the **lowest line number** (nothing runs). A line has at most one problem. The reasons:

| reason | when |
|---|---|
| `unknown directive` | the first word is not a directive of this language |
| `bad state` | a `state` line with the wrong shape or an invalid name |
| `duplicate state` | a second declaration of an already declared state |
| `bad initial` | an `initial` line with the wrong shape or an invalid name |
| `duplicate initial` | a second valid `initial` line |
| `outside state` | a `case`, `enter` or `exit` line before the first valid `state` line |
| `bad transition` | a transition line that does not have the shape above (missing words, invalid names, wrong arrow or action separator word, bad guard) |
| `bad action` | an action list that is empty (also `!` followed by nothing) or has an empty or malformed action, in a transition or in an `enter`/`exit` line |
| `unknown state` | a reference (`initial`, a transition target or a parent) to a state that is declared nowhere in the definition; reported on the line of the reference |
| `parent cycle` | the state's chain of parents comes back to a state already visited (a state that is its own parent, or two states that are each other's ancestors); reported on the declaration line of each state of the cycle |

For a transition line, shape problems (`bad transition`) are judged first and the action list (`bad action`) afterwards. A line that causes `bad state`, `duplicate state`, `bad transition` or `bad action` is ignored otherwise (it declares nothing). If there are no line problems but no `initial` line at all, the result is `error: no initial state`.

## Running

`events` is text split into events at blanks (spaces, tabs, newlines); any word is an event name (no validation). The machine starts by *entering* the initial state (the `enter` actions of its ancestors, outermost first, then its own), then handles each event in turn:

1. The transitions of the current state are examined in declaration order; the **first** one with the right event whose guard (if any) is true fires. If none of them fires, the transitions of its parent are examined the same way, then those of its grandparent, and so on. If no transition fires at all, the event is *ignored* (nothing changes).
2. A transition that fires moves the machine from the current state `S` to `TARGET` (the transition may be declared in an ancestor of `S`, but the machine always leaves from `S`). Guards use the counter values from *before* the step.
3. **Exits and enters.** Let `L` be the lowest state that is a *proper* ancestor of both `S` and `TARGET` (there may be none). The machine leaves `S`, then its parent, and so on **up to but not including** `L`, running each state's `exit` actions in that order (innermost first). Then the transition's own actions run. Then it enters the states on the path from just below `L` down to `TARGET` (outermost first), running their `enter` actions. So a transition to the current state leaves and re-enters it, and a transition to an ancestor leaves the state and re-enters the ancestor.

## Trace

The result is lines joined by `\n` (no trailing newline):

* first `start: -> INITIAL`;
* then one line per event, `EVENT: S -> TARGET` when a transition fired and `EVENT: ignored` otherwise;
* a line that ran any `emit` actions (during entering at the start, or during the step) ends with ` | ` and the emitted names separated by single spaces, in the order they were emitted;
* last `final STATE` followed, for every counter that was ever the subject of `set`, `inc` or `dec` (even if its value is 0 again), by ` NAME=VALUE`, sorted by name in ascending byte order.

## Interface

Implement this function in `lib/statemachine.rb` (module `Statemachine`):

```
Statemachine.machine(definition, events)
```

* `definition`: the machine definition text
* `events`: the events, separated by blanks
* returns the trace text, or an `error: ...` line.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

Definition:

```
initial dark
state dark
  case dusk => warming ! emit beep
state warming
  case dawn => dark
```

Events: `dusk warm dawn`

Result:

```
start: -> dark
dusk: dark -> warming | beep
warm: ignored
dawn: warming -> dark
final dark
```

Definition:

```
state flash
  case dawn => flash
initial flash
  case warm => beam
  case dawn => flash ! emit open
state failsafe < flash
  enter emit hum, inc tries
  case fog => beam ! dec hits, inc count
  case dawn => beam
  case dawn if hits != 1 => failsafe ! inc n 3
state beam
  case dawn => failsafe
  case dusk if count <= -2 => beam ! emit ok
  case warm if count != 2 => beam ! inc n
```

Events: `warm fog warm warm fog fog`

Result:

```
start: -> flash
warm: flash -> beam
fog: ignored
warm: beam -> beam
warm: beam -> beam
fog: ignored
fog: ignored
final beam n=2
```

Definition:

```
initial flash
state flash
  exit emit log
  case spin if hits > 4 => failsafe ! emit hum
  case spin => flash ! emit close
state dark < flash
  exit emit alert, emit reset
  case spin => failsafe
state failsafe
  enter emit flash, emit beep
  case spin if tries == 2 => dark ! emit hum
  case spin => failsafe
  case dusk => beam ! emit notify
state beam < flash
  enter inc count 1, set hits -3
  exit emit ok
  case dawn => flash
  case spin if hits >= -1 => beam ! emit bad
```

Events: `spin dusk dawn warm cut dawn spin`

Result:

```
start: -> flash
spin: flash -> flash | log close
dusk: ignored
dawn: ignored
warm: ignored
cut: ignored
dawn: ignored
spin: flash -> flash | log close
final flash
```

The definition language is invented (arrow `=>`, transition word `case`) so don't assume anything from other state-machine tools. It also has counters with guards and enter/exit actions and parent states with inherited transitions.
